title: Choose the yaw-moment model
brief: Model an asymmetric-thrust disturbance and connect it to the correct effector. Read the supplied effector map and distinguish yaw from pitch and roll.
supplied: For a separate twin-engine utility aircraft, can 8.6 kN m of usable opposing rudder/vertical-tail moment balance the yaw disturbance after losing 2.4 kN thrust at a 3.1 m lateral offset?
deltaT=2400 N of lost thrust magnitude; y=3.1 m perpendicular lateral arm about the CG; available=8600 N m opposing yaw-moment magnitude. This is not the trainer aircraft.
Required yaw-moment magnitude (N m), available-minus-required margin (N m), and the appropriate primary effector.

Offset thrust creates yaw demand. Rudder primarily controls yaw but may couple to roll; ailerons primarily roll and can cause adverse yaw. Elevator primarily pitches. Flaps change lift/drag and pitching moment; spoilers change lift/drag and may roll; propulsion contributes forces and moments. These are dominant, not exclusive, responses.
Static yaw balance only. No proof of engine-out controllability, bank limits, transient response, or minimum control speed.
Doubling lost thrust at fixed arm doubles yaw demand and reduces margin.
2400×3.1=7440 N m required; 8600−7440=1160 N m nominal margin.
Zero loss → zero demand; 2400 N loss →7440 N m; 4800 N loss →14880 N m.
Plot yaw demand against lost thrust and compare with 8600 N m capacity; identify the yaw effector and the sign/magnitude convention.
For each deltaT, evaluate your expression using y=3.1; compare its result with deltaT*y. The capacity line remains 8600 N m.
Retain only the nominal static yaw screen; investigate coupling, actuator limits, and uncertainty before an operational claim.

fields.label: Explain the reasoning for physics model

checks.message: Lost thrust 0 N at 3.1 m must give 0 N m yaw demand.
Lost thrust 2400 N at 3.1 m must give 7440 N m yaw demand.
Lost thrust 4800 N at 3.1 m must give 14880 N m yaw demand.
Select the yaw effector; identify roll coupling in your explanation.

hints: A thrust loss off the centerline creates a moment about the CG.
Multiply force magnitude by the perpendicular lateral arm; the result is in N m.
Use deltaT*y. Rudder primarily opposes yaw; do not use elevator pitch authority as evidence for this case.

sweep.units: Lost thrust in N; yaw moment in N m.
